title: Collections Standard — Late Charges on Interest Bills and Their Waiver, Operating Lines of Credit
content:
On the Operating Lines of Credit a late charge arises only on an interest bill, and only once the bill's grace period has run out.

## Clauses in force

1. **Timing.** A late charge may be assessed only after more than the product's grace days have passed since the due date of the interest bill, counted as calendar days with the due date itself as day 0, so the charge first arises on the day after the last grace day.
2. **Booking.** The late charge is booked as a fee charge with the late charge fee code whose source is that bill.
3. **One per bill.** Only one late charge may be assessed per interest bill.
4. **What carries no late charge.** No late charge applies to principal, to fees, or to matured principal, which carries the post-maturity rate instead.
5. **Error-correction waiver.** A late charge is waived on the basis of error correction when the record shows a payment effective on or before the last grace day that fully paid the bill.
6. **Courtesy waiver.** Otherwise, on the member's request, a late charge may be waived as a courtesy only when its interest bill has since been paid in full and the line has fewer courtesy waivers in the rolling window than the product's courtesy allowance. The rolling window is the 12 months ending on the date of the waiver being considered, running from the same calendar date one year earlier (exclusive) through that date (inclusive).
7. **One waiver per fee.** Only one waiver may be booked per fee assessment, and only for its unpaid amount.

What has been paid on a bill is the interest payments applied to that bill less any of those payments later returned unpaid. Whether a late charge or a waiver already exists for a bill or an assessment is read from the line's own transaction record before a new one is booked.

## Clauses no longer in force

- "It is charged on an interest bill whose billed amount is not fully paid by then (what has been paid on the bill below the bill amount)" — no longer in force; superseded by the current basis for which bill carries the charge.
- "at the product's late charge percentage of the unpaid billed interest, no less than the product's minimum late charge and no more than its maximum late charge, rounded to cents," — no longer in force; superseded by the current basis for the amount of the charge.

## Grace boundary (hypothetical bill due 15 January, 15 grace days)

| Date | Days after the due date | Late charge may be assessed |
|---|---|---|
| 15 January | 0 (the due date) | No |
| 30 January | 15 (the last grace day) | No |
| 31 January | 16 | Yes — the first day the charge arises |

## Waiver judgement (hypothetical, courtesy allowance of 1)

| Bill paid in full | Courtesy waivers on the line in the rolling window | Courtesy waiver on request |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | 0 | May be granted |
| Yes | 1 | Not available |
| No | 0 | Not available |

A payment effective on 30 January that fully paid the bill in the grace example above would instead ground an error-correction waiver of a charge booked on 31 January.

superseded_clauses: at late_charge_pct of the unpaid billed interest, no less than late_charge_min_usd and no more than late_charge_max_usd, rounded to cents,
